Sun.title: Sun
Sun.extract: The Sun is the G2V yellow dwarf star at the center of the Solar System. Containing 99.86% of the system's mass, its core fuses 600 million tons of hydrogen into helium every second.

Moon.title: Moon
Moon.extract: The Moon is Earth's only natural satellite, orbiting at a mean distance of 384,400 km. Tidally locked to Earth, its surface features dark basaltic maria and ancient cratered highlands.

Mercury.title: Mercury (planet)
Mercury.extract: Mercury is the innermost and smallest planet in the Solar System, orbiting the Sun every 88 days. Its heavily cratered, airless surface experiences extreme temperature swings from -180 °C to +430 °C.

Venus.title: Venus
Venus.extract: Venus is the second planet from the Sun and the brightest natural object in Earth's night sky after the Moon (reaching mag -4.9). Its dense CO2 atmosphere drives a runaway greenhouse effect at 465 °C.

Mars.title: Mars
Mars.extract: Mars is the fourth planet from the Sun, colored rusty red by iron oxide dust. It hosts Olympus Mons (the largest volcano in the Solar System at 21.9 km), Valles Marineris, and seasonal polar ice caps.

Jupiter.title: Jupiter
Jupiter.extract: Jupiter is the largest planet in the Solar System, a gas giant banded with ammonia cloud zones and belts, the iconic Great Red Spot storm, and the four Galilean moons: Io, Europa, Ganymede, and Callisto.

Saturn.title: Saturn
Saturn.extract: Saturn is the sixth planet from the Sun, renowned for its brilliant ring system of water-ice particles split by the Cassini Division, and accompanied by major moons including Titan, Rhea, and Enceladus.

Uranus.title: Uranus
Uranus.extract: Uranus is the seventh planet from the Sun, an ice giant discovered by William Herschel in 1781. Methane in its upper atmosphere gives it a cyan-blue hue, and its axial tilt is an extreme 97.8°.

Neptune.title: Neptune
Neptune.extract: Neptune is the eighth and farthest known planet from the Sun (30.1 AU), discovered in 1846 from Urbain Le Verrier's mathematical predictions. This deep-blue ice giant hosts supersonic winds and the moon Triton.

Io.title: Io (moon)
Io.extract: Io is the innermost Galilean moon of Jupiter and the most volcanically active world in the Solar System, driven by intense tidal heating.

Europa.title: Europa (moon)
Europa.extract: Europa is an icy Galilean moon of Jupiter whose fractured water-ice crust conceals a global subsurface liquid saltwater ocean.

Ganymede.title: Ganymede (moon)
Ganymede.extract: Ganymede is the largest moon in the Solar System (5,268 km diameter, larger than Mercury) and the only satellite known to possess its own intrinsic magnetic field.

Callisto.title: Callisto (moon)
Callisto.extract: Callisto is the outermost Galilean moon of Jupiter, featuring an ancient, heavily cratered icy surface dominated by the multi-ring Valhalla basin.

Titan.title: Titan (moon)
Titan.extract: Titan is Saturn's largest moon and the only moon with a dense nitrogen-methane atmosphere and stable surface lakes and seas of liquid hydrocarbons.
